AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities 9 3.2 Disinfecting Clothing and Household Art? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities 9 3.2 Disinfecting Clothing and Household Art.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities 9 3.2 Disinfecting Clothing and Household Art.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities 9 3.2 Disinfecting Clothing and Household Art.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities 9 3.2 Disinfecting Clothing and Household Art.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Animal Feed: Hay? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning Waste Disposal Facilities.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Integrated Farming? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Integrated Farming.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Integrated Farming.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Integrated Farming.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Integrated Farming.

12. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

14. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Leftover Food? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Leftover Food.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Leftover Food.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Leftover Food.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Leftover Food.

16. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
